public_rationale: The evidence supports a broad wave of generative AI litigation in 2024 across developers and creative sectors [e1–e4]. Counsel announced new journalism lawsuits against OpenAI on February 28, 2024 [e3]. Record companies filed their complaint against Suno on June 24, 2024 [e2]. The July 25, 2024 review reported roughly 25 active lawsuits, including cases filed before 2024 [e1]. The retrospective published January 9, 2025 identifies new 2024 author suits against Databricks and Anthropic, alongside proceedings in existing cases [e4]. Together, these records support litigation's breadth and sustained activity during 2024 [e1–e4].
limitations: “The year of” supplies no numerical threshold; support follows the contract's ordinary reading of substantial, sustained litigation.
The active-case count includes earlier filings and is not a count of new 2024 suits.
The packet does not establish worldwide totals, year-over-year growth, or a record-setting year.
The cited complaints establish allegations and litigation activity, not proven infringement.

from_speaker: will be the year of Generative AI litigation
our_interpretation: The ordinary reading is that litigation would become a prominent, sustained feature of the generative AI industry during 2024, with substantial new filings and proceedings across multiple developers.
The copyright-focused context makes disputes over training material and generated outputs central examples.
The claim does not specify a lawsuit count, growth percentage, plaintiff victory, or final judgment.
The phrase does not require 2024 to exceed every earlier or later year. Existing cases count as proceedings, but are not counted as new 2024 filings.
criteria.support_condition: Dated filings and proceedings establish a substantial wave of generative AI litigation in 2024 across multiple developers and categories of rights holders, corroborated by a broader litigation review.
criteria.contradiction_condition: A reasonably comprehensive record shows only isolated generative AI litigation and little substantive activity during 2024, rather than the predicted prominence and breadth.
